subject: Clarify headroom policy for Dedicated pilot + rollout timeline
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@orionhealth.com, eng@cloudops.partner
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify headroom policy for Dedicated pilot + rollout timeline

Team —

Orion Health wants to accelerate their dedicated pilot and is asking for a temporary headroom carve (additional 3x slots) for a 4-week soak during their integration testing. They flagged a go/no-go tied to our ability to guarantee short-term capacity for early July.

Two asks from my side:
- Can Ops safely grant a 4-week headroom bump (3 additional GPU slots) without impacting Q3 commitments?
- If yes, what are the guardrails (SLA, eviction notice, telemetry we need) and what is the minimal lead time to schedule?

I've attached the headroom request form from Orion and a draft pilot runbook — the runbook has their expected traffic profile.

High-level constraints we should consider: we promised predictable throughput to two enterprise pilots in July (one of which is Atlas Health). We need to avoid cascading preemption.

Goal: decide by EOD Thu so we can confirm timelines with Orion (they want an onboarding date window).

Thanks,
Kimberly
(Head of Product — Dedicated)

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify headroom policy for Dedicated pilot + rollout timeline

On Tue, Jun 9, 2026 at 08:12 AM kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
>
> Orion Health wants to accelerate their dedicated pilot and is asking for a temporary headroom carve...

Short answer: probably, with constraints.

Operational facts:
- Current pool utilization for the US enterprise cluster is 78% daytime average; projected July reservations (committed) will push expected peak to ~92% if all pilots start as planned.
- We have a small buffer (approx 6 slots) that is usually consumed by burst lanes; asking for +3 for 4 weeks is doable if we:
  1) enforce strict burst throttling (no more than 20% of carved slots used for batch runs)
  2) provision a 48-hour eviction notice window for any preemption needs
  3) require Orion to keep a static model version during the soak (no heavy hyperparameter sweeps)

Operational lead time: 72 hours to schedule and provision once we sign off (longer if we need cross-region mapping).

I'll attach a short checklist for runbook requirements and telemetry hooks. We need PM to confirm the expected token/sec and concurrency targets to compute cost impact.

—Laura
Principal Infra PM
[Attachment: ops_checklist_headroom.pdf]

From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify headroom policy for Dedicated pilot + rollout timeline

Thanks Laura — that matches my risk read. A couple of product-level clarifications: 

- If we grant headroom, product wants a hard guardrail on model size/quantization profile (we should limit to 70B quantized variants for the pilot) so kernel selection and memory curves are predictable.
- We should gate the exception on a short-term SLA (72h support response, but explicit no-guarantee on P99 latency until the soak is complete).
- Can we require a compensated pilot fee or billable temporary uplift? Ops — what is the minimal chargeback we can push through procurement? We need to ensure this doesn't create a precedent of free extended headroom.

Proposed decision path:
1) Approve one-time +3 slots for 4 weeks, contingent on Ops checklist, static model version, and a temporary uplift fee.
2) Reassess metrics at weeks 1 and 3; abort if we see >15% increase in preemption events or 10% regression in latency.

Marcus
Sr. PM — Dedicated

On Wed, Jun 10, 2026 at 09:03 AM laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll add an expected telemetry list to the drive link.

From: procure@orionhealth.com <procure@orionhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@cloudops.partner
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 07:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify headroom policy for Dedicated pilot + rollout timeline

Hi Kimberly / Grace —

Thanks for the quick follow-up. From Orion's side:
- We confirm the soak will be limited to inference traffic with a capped concurrency of 12 and peak token/sec as listed in the runbook attachment.
- We are okay with a temporary uplift fee. Procurement would prefer a short addendum rather than a new invoice line item.
- We can commit to a locked model version and no hyperparameter sweeps during the 4-week window.

Please share the uplift amount and the runbook checklist so procurement can sign the addendum.

Regards,
Jae Park
Procurement Lead — Orion Health
[Attachment: signed_headroom_request_form.pdf]

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, procure@orionhealth.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify headroom policy for Dedicated pilot + rollout timeline

Appreciate the fast turn here — decision: APPROVE under the following conditions.

Decision summary (approved):
- One-time +3 GPU slots for a 4-week soak starting earliest Mon, 05 Jul 2026 and latest Wed, 07 Jul 2026 (Ops to confirm exact start after scheduling).
- Guardrails required before start: ops_checklist_headroom.pdf items complete, attached telemetry configured (P50/P95/P99, preemption count, slot occupancy), and model/version locked.
- Billing: temporary uplift equal to 25% of list dedicated rate for the additional slots, invoiced as an addendum (procurement OK with addendum).
- Abort criteria: automatic termination if >15% increase in preemptions or sustained 10% regression in P99 latency vs baseline; product/ops to validate at days 7 and 21.

Action items: 
- Laura: finalize schedule and checklist, confirm provisioning ETA (72 hours) 
- Marcus/Kim: send final runbook with token/sec and concurrency numbers into the shared drive and mark item INF-2421 for metric gating
- Procurement (Orion): return signed addendum by Fri EOD (11 Jun) to lock dates

I'll own the exec notification and ensure this doesn't erode our precedent. If anyone disagrees, speak now. Otherwise I'll confirm with Orion and loop in finance for the invoice addendum.

-Grace
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: approval_headroom_addendum_template.docx]
